sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Create an SVG logo for a generative AI company using organic shapes and neutral tones

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.12.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Loam identity. Pure SVG geometry; no fonts or third-party packages.

Run: python3 build_logo.py
Optional macOS PNG export: python3 build_logo.py --png

The three unfurling seed shapes use the same Bezier geometry rotated 120°.
All wordmark letters and the small-cap descriptor are custom vector paths.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import subprocess
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / 'output'
PAPER = '#F4F1EA'
INK = '#353A32'
ASH = '#595F52'
STONE = '#999585'
OAT = '#C2B6A2'
MUTED = '#737468'

# A curled seed: full rounded outer contour, open counter, tapered growth tip.
SEED = ('M 9 -23 '
        'C -12 -37 -41 -48 -57 -75 '
        'C -82 -118 -56 -158 -15 -162 '
        'C 39 -167 98 -118 103 -75 '
        'C 108 -41 81 -10 51 -10 '
        'C 43 -10 36 -13 33 -20 '
        'C 28 -31 36 -42 48 -50 '
        'C 64 -61 66 -77 55 -90 '
        'C 42 -106 18 -111 0 -107 '
        'C -19 -103 -29 -92 -27 -76 '
        'C -24 -58 -4 -42 11 -24 '
        'Q 14 -20 9 -23 Z')

# Custom lowercase lettering. Counters use the even-odd fill rule.
LETTERS = [
    (0, 'M 0 0 H 27 V 151 C 27 164 33 170 46 170 H 56 V 194 H 43 '
        'C 15 194 0 178 0 152 Z'),
    (79, 'M 68 54 C 107 54 133 82 133 125 '
         'C 133 169 108 197 68 197 C 28 197 2 169 2 125 '
         'C 2 82 28 54 68 54 Z '
         'M 68 78 C 43 78 28 95 28 125 C 28 156 43 173 68 173 '
         'C 92 173 107 156 107 125 C 107 95 92 78 68 78 Z'),
    (242, 'M 64 54 C 84 54 100 62 110 75 V 57 H 136 V 194 H 111 V 176 '
          'C 100 190 84 197 64 197 C 26 197 0 169 0 126 '
          'C 0 83 26 54 64 54 Z '
          'M 68 78 C 43 78 26 96 26 126 C 26 155 42 173 68 173 '
          'C 94 173 110 155 110 126 C 110 96 94 78 68 78 Z'),
    (410, 'M 0 57 H 25 V 75 C 34 61 47 54 65 54 '
          'C 87 54 102 63 110 80 C 120 63 137 54 157 54 '
          'C 190 54 209 77 209 114 V 194 H 182 V 117 '
          'C 182 91 173 79 154 79 C 134 79 121 94 121 119 V 194 H 94 V 117 '
          'C 94 91 85 79 65 79 C 44 79 27 95 27 120 V 194 H 0 Z'),
]

# A quiet, letter-spaced single-line alphabet for the descriptor.
CAPS = {
    'A': 'M 0 10 L 3.5 0 L 7 10 M 1.3 6.5 H 5.7',
    'C': 'M 7 1.2 C 6.2 .4 5.2 0 3.7 0 C 1.2 0 0 1.9 0 5 '
         'C 0 8.1 1.2 10 3.7 10 C 5.2 10 6.2 9.6 7 8.8',
    'E': 'M 6.6 0 H 0 V 10 H 6.6 M 0 4.8 H 5.5',
    'G': 'M 7 1.2 C 6.2 .4 5.2 0 3.7 0 C 1.2 0 0 1.9 0 5 '
         'C 0 8.1 1.2 10 3.7 10 C 5.1 10 6.2 9.6 7 8.8 V 5.5 H 4',
    'I': 'M 0 0 V 10',
    'L': 'M 0 0 V 10 H 6.4',
    'N': 'M 0 10 V 0 L 7 10 V 0',
    'R': 'M 0 10 V 0 H 3.6 C 5.7 0 6.8 1 6.8 2.8 '
         'C 6.8 4.6 5.7 5.5 3.6 5.5 H 0 M 3.6 5.5 L 7.2 10',
    'T': 'M 0 0 H 7.6 M 3.8 0 V 10',
    'V': 'M 0 0 L 3.5 10 L 7 0',
}


def emblem(x, y, scale=1, mono=None):
    colors = [mono] * 3 if mono else [ASH, STONE, OAT]
    paths = '\n'.join(
        f'<path fill="{color}" transform="rotate({angle})" d="{SEED}"/>'
        for color, angle in zip(colors, (0, 120, 240)))
    return f'<g transform="translate({x} {y}) scale({scale})">{paths}</g>'


def wordmark(x, y, scale=1, color=INK):
    paths = '\n'.join(f'<path transform="translate({offset} 0)" d="{d}"/>'
                      for offset, d in LETTERS)
    return (f'<g fill="{color}" fill-rule="evenodd" '
            f'transform="translate({x} {y}) scale({scale})">{paths}</g>')


def descriptor(x, y, scale=1.4):
    position = 0
    parts = []
    for char in 'GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE':
        if char == ' ':
            position += 6
            continue
        parts.append(f'<path transform="translate({position:g} 0)" d="{CAPS[char]}"/>')
        position += 5.2 if char == 'I' else 11.9
    return (f'<g transform="translate({x} {y}) scale({scale})" '
            f'fill="none" stroke="{MUTED}" stroke-width=".85" '
            'stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round">'
            + ''.join(parts) + '</g>')


def svg(width, height, title, description, content):
    return (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}" '
            f'viewBox="0 0 {width} {height}" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc">\n'
            f'<title id="title">{title}</title>\n<desc id="desc">{description}</desc>\n'
            f'{content}\n</svg>\n')


def build():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    story = ('Loam, a generative AI company. Three unfurling organic seed shapes '
             'form a continuous cycle of growth, in ash, warm stone and oat. '
             'A custom lowercase wordmark balances the symbol.')
    hero = (f'<rect width="1600" height="1000" fill="{PAPER}"/>\n'
            + emblem(463, 503)
            + wordmark(667, 389)
            + descriptor(670, 627))
    (OUT / 'loam-presentation.svg').write_text(
        svg(1600, 1000, 'loam — generative intelligence', story, hero))

    lockup = emblem(188, 201) + wordmark(392, 87) + descriptor(395, 325)
    (OUT / 'loam-logo.svg').write_text(
        svg(1050, 400, 'loam — primary logo', story + ' Transparent background.', lockup))

    (OUT / 'loam-symbol.svg').write_text(
        svg(400, 400, 'loam — organic seed symbol', story + ' Transparent background.',
            emblem(200, 206)))


def render_png():
    """Render via macOS Quick Look and crop its square preview to the artboard.

    The temporary SVG uses percentage dimensions to avoid retina viewport clipping.
    All temporary files live in this directory and are automatically removed.
    """
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='.render-', dir=ROOT) as temp:
        temp = Path(temp)
        source = (OUT / 'loam-presentation.svg').read_text()
        source = source.replace('width="1600" height="1000" viewBox',
                                'width="100%" height="100%" viewBox', 1)
        preview = temp / 'loam.svg'
        preview.write_text(source)
        subprocess.run(['qlmanage', '-t', '-s', '1600', '-o', str(temp), str(preview)],
                       check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-hide_banner', '-loglevel', 'error', '-y',
                        '-i', str(temp / 'loam.svg.png'),
                        '-vf', 'crop=1600:1000:0:300', '-frames:v', '1',
                        str(OUT / 'loam-presentation.png')], check=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--png', action='store_true', help='also render a PNG using macOS Quick Look')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    build()
    if args.png:
        render_png()
    for file in sorted(OUT.iterdir()):
        print(f'{file.relative_to(ROOT)} ({file.stat().st_size:,} bytes)')

from pathlib import Path
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import struct
out = Path('output')
files = list(out.iterdir())
assert len(files) <= 8
for p in sorted(files):
    assert p.stat().st_size < 2_000_000
    if p.suffix == '.svg':
        root = ET.parse(p).getroot()
        assert root.attrib['viewBox']
        assert not root.findall('.//{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}text')
        assert not root.findall('.//{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}image')
        print(p, root.attrib['viewBox'], 'standalone vector / no font dependencies')
    elif p.suffix == '.png':
        data = p.read_bytes()
        assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
        w,h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
        assert (w,h) == (1600,1000)
        print(p, f'{w}×{h}', 'PNG verified')
PY
